raw_text:
Ever wondered why your fingers and toes get all pruney after a long bath or swim? It's not just your skin soaking up water like a sponge! Scientists think it's actually an evolutionary feature controlled by your nervous system.

When your hands are in water for a while, your nerves trigger blood vessels in your fingertips to constrict. This causes the skin to pucker and wrinkle. The current theory is that this gives us better grip on wet or submerged objects—like a built-in rain tread for your fingers! It's a pretty cool trick our bodies have developed.

So next time you see those wrinkles, remember: it's your nervous system hard at work, not just soggy skin.

raw_text:
Ever catch yourself thinking, "Well, I already paid for it" or "I've put so much time into this" as a reason to stick with something that's clearly not working? That's the sunk-cost fallacy in action.

It's the idea that past investments—money, time, effort—should dictate our future choices. But here’s the thing: that money is already spent. That time is already gone. Whether you push forward or walk away, you can't get it back.

The only question that really matters is: "Going forward, from this moment, is this still the best choice?" Letting go of a bad plan isn't wasting what you put in; it's refusing to waste even more. Don't throw good time or money after bad just because you're already invested. Sometimes, the smartest move is to cut your losses and choose a better path.
